cards: Utu-hengal was a king of Uruk in the late 22nd century BCE who led the Sumerian cities against the Gutians.
r. c. 2120 BCE · Ancient Near East
Gudea was a ruler of the Sumerian city-state of Lagash around 2100 BCE, in the period between the fall of the Akkadian Empire and the rise of the Third Dynasty of Ur.
r. c. 2100 BCE · Ancient Near East
Kutik-Inshushinak (also read Puzur-Inshushinak) was the last king of the Awan dynasty of Elam, ruling around 2100 BCE.
r. c. 2100 BCE · Ancient Near East
Tirigan was the last Gutian king listed in the Sumerian King List, said to have reigned for only forty days.
r. c. 2120 BCE · Ancient Near East
Yu the Great is the legendary Chinese ruler said to have tamed the great flood by dredging channels rather than building dams, and to have founded the Xia dynasty.
traditionally c. 2100 BCE · Central & East Asia
Intef I was a ruler of Thebes in Upper Egypt in the late 22nd century BCE, the first of the Eleventh Dynasty to claim the full titles of a king.
r. c. 2134–2117 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Mentuhotep I was a nomarch of Thebes in Upper Egypt in the late 22nd century BCE and the founder of the Eleventh Dynasty.
late 22nd century BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Meryibre Khety, often counted as Khety I, was the founder of the Ninth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Herakleopolis Magna in the First Intermediate Period.
c. 22nd century BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Neferkauhor was a king of the Eighth Dynasty of Egypt who reigned briefly at Memphis late in the 22nd century BCE.
late 22nd century BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Qakare Ibi was a king of Egypt's Eighth Dynasty in the First Intermediate Period, known from the Abydos king list.
c. 22nd century BCE · Egypt & North Africa
